topics.title: The chance meeting and the invitation to Foyot's

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how the story is framed as a flashback triggered by a meeting at the play twenty years later.
Describe the young narrator's poor circumstances and why flattery made him accept the luncheon.

topics.title: At the restaurant: salmon, caviare and Champagne

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the gap between the guest's claims about eating little and what she actually orders.
Explain how the narrator hides his alarm about money behind polite hospitality.

topics.title: The giant asparagus and the narrator's panic

concepts.learning_objective: Interpret the narrator's growing panic as the guest orders the expensive asparagus.
Analyse the comic exaggeration and imagery used to describe the guest eating.
Recall how the peaches and the bill leave the narrator penniless for the month.
Interpret the narrator's parting retort and the guest's reply calling him a humorist.

topics.title: The ending: revenge, irony and humour

concepts.learning_objective: Explain the ironic 'revenge' in the final line, when the guest weighs twenty-one stone.
Identify instances of irony and self-mocking humour in the story.
Evaluate how the first-person narrative heightens the story's effects.

topics.title: The author and the language of the story

concepts.learning_objective: Recall key facts about William Somerset Maugham's life, works and style.
Infer the meanings of words such as mortifying, vindictive, complacency and ingratiating from context.
